skeleton:
Bubble-and-Squeak Cakes

British · Easy · Makes 8 cakes (serves 4)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The bubble and squeak master's individual form: the leftover mash-and-cabbage mix shaped into palm-sized cakes, each one crusted on both faces and served as a self-contained unit — the component that turns a fry-up plate modular. Where the whole-pan bubble is a wedge cut from a shared disc, the cake is its own object: crusted edges on every side, a higher crust-to-middle ratio, and the Cheddar option folded in where the big cake would never dare. The small format has its own technique, distinct enough from the master to earn this record: the cakes are shaped smaller and pressed firmer (fragility scales inversely with size), the fry runs hotter and shorter (more edge, less middle to heat through), and the cakes freeze raw in stacks — the make-ahead breakfast component the site's freezers have been waiting for.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The cakes

For frying

  • small cakes fry hotter than the big disc)

To serve

  • see Variations
- **The master's laws, restated:** cold dry potato, squeezed-dry cabbage, and a firm press at shaping. At small scale the press matters double — a 100 g cake has proportionally more edge to hold than a 500 g disc, and edges are where loose cakes shed. - **Chop the cabbage finer than the master's** — coarse cabbage shreds tear a small cake's structure apart at the edge. Finely chopped, it integrates and the cakes keep clean rims. - **The 20-minute chill** — non-negotiable at any size, and it is what lets these flip with a single spatula rather than the master's plate manoeuvre.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Shaping: 2 cm thick, pressed firm, cracked rims re-pressed before the chill.
  • First side: 3 undisturbed minutes at medium to a freckled deep gold.
  • Second side: 2–3 minutes, cheese laced and caught at the edges, no pale bands.
  • Centre: each cake steaming hot throughout, centre held at 75 °C for 30 seconds; crust audibly crackles, middle soft and Cheddar-flecked.

Bubble-and-Squeak Cakes

Prep: 15 minutes, plus 20 minutes chilling · Cook: 15 minutes · Total: 50 minutes · Makes 8 cakes (serves 4)

Ingredients

The cakes

  • 500 g cold cooked floury potatoes, roughly mashed
  • 200 g cold cooked cabbage or Brussels sprouts, squeezed very dry, finely chopped
  • 30 g butter, softened
  • 50 g mature Cheddar, grated (the small-format luxury the big cake can't carry)
  • 2 spring onions, finely sliced (30 g)
  • 3 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper
  • 0.5 g grated nutmeg

For frying

  • 30 g butter plus 15 ml neutral oil (the oil buffer — small cakes fry hotter than the big disc)

To serve

  • Brown breakfast sauce, poached or fried eggs, or the breakfast muffin build — see Variations
  • 8 cakes serve 4 as a component, 2 as a light meal

Instructions

  1. **Mix and shape.** Combine everything through the nutmeg until the mix holds when squeezed. Divide into 8 (about 110 g each) and shape into rounds 7–8 cm across and 2 cm thick, pressing each firmly between cupped palms. Chill 20 minutes. Checkpoint — each cake holds a clean, crisp edge and lifts off the board intact; the surface is matte and compact. Any cake that cracks at the rim gets re-pressed — a cracked rim is a crumbled cake in the pan.
  2. **Fry hot-ish and short — 3 minutes a side.** Heat the butter and oil in a large pan over medium heat until foaming. Fry the cakes in one uncrowded layer (two batches if needed), 3 minutes undisturbed to a deep gold crust, then flip each with a single confident turn and give 2–3 minutes more. Hold finished cakes in a low oven (about 120 °C) while the second batch runs. Checkpoint — both faces deep golden with darker lacy edges where the cheese caught, the sides showing no raw ring, and each cake steaming hot throughout, with its centre held at 75 °C for 30 seconds on a clean food thermometer. The small format browns faster than the master's disc — medium, not medium-low, and watch the second side.
  3. **Serve hot, sauced, or stacked.** The cakes land beside the eggs as the potato component, or become the plate themselves: two cakes, a poached egg, sauce over — the brunch presentation. Checkpoint — the eating test: an audible crust under the fork, then the soft Cheddar-flecked middle, the cabbage sweet at the caramelised rim — the master's flavour at a higher crust pitch.

Finish & Plate

As the fry-up's potato component beside the eggs, or as the foundation plate: two cakes per person, a poached or fried egg draped across, brown sauce or the breakfast chutney at the side, and a mug of tea. However they land, eat them while the crust still talks — the small format's crust is the dish's whole voice, and it softens to a murmur within minutes.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Cakes crumbled at the flipUnder-pressed, under-chilled, or coarse cabbageFirm press, 20-minute chill, finely chopped cabbage
Cheese burnt before the crust setHeat too high for the cheese's sugarsMedium, and the second side shorter than the first
Pale, soft cakesPan crowded or fat too shallowOne layer, a proper foaming film of butter and oil
Raw ring at the sidesCakes too thick2 cm maximum — these are crust vehicles, not blocks

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **The make-ahead champion:** freeze the shaped uncooked cakes for up to 2 months on a tray, then bag them. Cook from frozen over medium-low until steaming hot throughout, checking the centre holds 75 °C for 30 seconds. Refrigerate the mix and use it within 2 days of originally cooking its ingredients. Reheat the cakes only once and serve straight away. - **Variation — the breakfast muffin's base:** one cake replaces the muffin in the breakfast muffin build, egg folded over the top — the handheld bubble. - **Variation — the smoked fish cake:** 100 g smoked haddock, flaked, folded through the mix — the kedgeree-adjacent deluxe, and a pub-lunch standard at heart. - **The family map:** the master (whole pan), these cakes (component), the fried-egg plate (foundation), and the benedict (brunch) — one recipe's four registers, all from the same leftovers.
